https://www.gazetteandherald.co.uk/news/.text: Europe’s wildfire crisis eases in west as danger shifts east to Greece By PA News Agency Share 0 Comments 2 Skip to next photo 1 / 1 Show caption 1 / 1 Share 0 Comments This article is brought to you by our exclusive subscriber partnership with our sister title USA Today, and has been written by our American colleagues. It does not necessarily reflect the view of The Herald. Europe’s wildfire emergency eased across much of western Europe on Saturday but its most dangerous front shifted to Greece, where gale-force winds drove flames through a seaside resort, forced hundreds to flee by sea and hampered firefighting aircraft. For Greece, the danger carried grim resonance: a 2018 wildfire at the seaside community of Mati, near Athens, killed 104 people, making it Europe’s deadliest wildfire this century. In south-western France, firefighters held a vast wildfire within its perimeter, with about 198,000 people now allowed home after what may have been the country’s largest peacetime evacuation. Major fires in Spain were also no longer advancing, and Portugal’s main blaze was under control. Flames burn through a forest during a wildfire near Porto Germeno (Michael Varaklas/AP) A second French fire stopped expanding overnight after racing across four square miles in six hours on Friday — “faster than a horse at full gallop”, according to the prefecture. But it remained active on Saturday and 2,500 people were still unable to return home. The gains in western Europe marked a sharp turn from the height of the crisis, when fires in France and Spain alone drove a third of a million people from homes and holiday sites, emptied towns during the summer tourism season and stretched firefighters, aircraft and emergency services across simultaneous emergencies. Europe is Earth’s fastest-warming continent, heating at more than twice the global average since the 1980s, according to the European Union’s Copernicus climate service. Rising temperatures and prolonged drought leave vegetation drier and more combustible, allowing fires to spread faster and burn more intensely. Nearly 500 firefighters battled on Saturday to protect Porto Germeno, a popular resort on the Gulf of Corinth, as flames tore through thick pine forest and smoke blocked out the sun. The fire broke out on Friday near the neighbouring coastal village of Agios Vasileios. About 300 people were evacuated by sea, and authorities issued further evacuation orders on Saturday. “A pristine forest, a paradise, was surrendered to the hands of the fire,” said Minas Tzortzanis, a 60-year-old farmer and local resident. “There are no words to explain what has happened. Destruction. Total destruction.” A firefighter works to extinguish fires in south-west France (Emma Da Silva/AP) Theodore Giannaros, a wildfire meteorologist at the National Observatory of Athens, estimated that 15 to 19 square miles had been affected. Authorities had not issued an official burned-area figure. The operation also included specialised forest-fire teams, crews temporarily deployed from France and Romania, 19 water-dropping planes and 11 helicopters. New fires erupted elsewhere in Greece. A blaze east of Nafpaktos prompted evacuation alerts for at least four villages. “The very strong to gale-force winds continue to create exceptionally difficult conditions,” climate crisis and civil protection minister Evangelos Tournas said. Extreme turbulence was preventing some aircraft from collecting water or approaching the fires closely enough to make drops, he said. The Gironde fire has burned 162 square miles of pine forest west of Bordeaux, an area four times the size of Paris. It remained contained within its perimeter on Saturday but had not been declared “fixed” — the point at which crews determine that a fire is no longer advancing. Active sectors and buried hot spots persisted. Authorities reopened more communities on Friday, but several remained largely deserted on Saturday. Much of the forested Cap Ferret peninsula stayed evacuated because a nearby hot spot could flare again. Flames burn through a forest in Greece (Michael Varaklas/AP) “Today, the fire is still not fixed. It is contained,” Lt Col Eric Pitault told reporters. Crews used tactical burns overnight. Along 149 miles of fire edge, heat could remain hidden underground and erupt again. In the Mediterranean Var region, defensive lines around the Gros Bessillon fire held overnight and no additional ground burned, Var prefect Simon Babre told French media on Saturday. The blaze had been declared fixed earlier in the week before mistral gusts revived embers on Friday and sent it racing through dry hills in temperatures approaching 42C. It remained active on Saturday, with 1,300 firefighters deployed and about 2,500 people still unable to return home. The fire’s sudden return “defies understanding”, Mr Babre said. Twenty French departments were under an orange heat warning on Saturday, mostly in the east and south-east. Eight departments faced a high forest-fire risk. For residents returning to the Gironde fire zone, the easing emergency brought a first reckoning with what had been lost. In Le Porge, one of the communities hardest hit, Matthieu Plessis returned on Saturday to the ruins of a home that had been in his family for seven generations. Just over a week earlier, smoke had turned the afternoon almost to night as flames raced along both sides of the road. Now the 40-year-old mechanic drove through blackened forest and struggled to identify what had once stood there. “There are little details here and there that I recognise, but otherwise everything is unrecognisable,” Mr Plessis said. “You don’t even know what was here anymore, or who lived where.” He had to force open the property’s gate because its key had burned. A chimney and twisted metal frames were among the few clues to where the rooms had been. The tools and machinery from his bicycle repair business were gone. “It’s not easy. I’m trying to stay strong and help other people now,” Mr Plessis said. “I don’t want to spend the next 10 years feeling sorry for myself.” Share 0 Comments Get involved with the news Send your news & photos Loading... Beállítom Vizsgálatot indított a ciprusi rendőrség Roman Abramovics pénzügyei miatt. A nyomozás azután indult, hogy a BBC Panorama című oknyomozó műsor feltárta: a Deloitte könyvvizsgáló és tanácsadó cég közreműködhetett dokumentumok meghamisításában, hogy elrejtsék az orosz oligarcha vagyonát, és ezzel segítsék az adóelkerülését – írta a BBC . A ciprusi igazságügyi minisztérium egyik tisztviselője a héten parlamenti képviselőknek azt mondta, hogy a BBC Panorama és a Bureau of Investigative Journalism (TBIJ) újságíró szervezet által feltárt információkat a rendőrség pénzügyi hírszerzési egysége is vizsgálja. Andreas Anastasiades, a ciprusi rendőrség képviselője a parlamenti képviselőknek megerősítette, hogy a rendőrség pénzügyi bűncselekményekkel foglalkozó egysége már megkezdte a bizonyítékok összegyűjtését. Hozzátette, hogy a vizsgálat várhatóan több hónapig tart majd. Abramovics ügyvédei azt közölték, hogy ügyfelük tagadja az adóelkerülésre és vagyona eltitkolására vonatkozó vádakat. Az ügyvédek szerint a BBC Panorama nem szolgáltatott bizonyítékot arra, hogy a milliárdos tudott volna bármilyen dokumentum meghamisításáról, vagy utasítást adott volna rá. Azt is hangsúlyozták, hogy Abramovics cégei jogszerűen támaszkodhattak szakértők tanácsaira. A Deloitte ciprusi leányvállalata azt nyilatkozta, hogy tevékenysége során „betartja a vonatkozó jogszabályokat”. Hozzátették, hogy nem tudnak nyilatkozni az ügyről, mivel az érintett dokumentumok több mint húszévesek, és már nem hozzáférhetőek. A BBC és a TBIJ múlt héten közzétett jelentése részletesen bemutatta, hogyan tűntek el Abramovics cégének könyveléséből 672 millió dollárt érő vagyonelemek, köztük luxusjachtok, villák és magánrepülőgépek. Mindez a Deloitte által Cipruson 2006-ban jóváhagyott beszámolókhoz kapcsolódott. A világ legnagyobb könyvvizsgáló és tanácsadó cégeként számon tartott Deloitte emellett egy olyan konstrukció kidolgozásában is közreműködhetett, amely dokumentumok meghamisításával segíthette az orosz oligarcha vagyonát terhelő jelentős adófizetési kötelezettség kijátszását. A bizonyítékok kiszivárgott iratokból származnak. A dokumentumokban több ezer, Abramovics pénzügyeire, valamint egy Ciprusról irányított offshore cégháló működésére vonatkozó feljegyzések vannak. Ez a hálózat 1995 és 2022 között működött. A BBC és médiapartnerei – köztük a TBIJ, a Guardian, a Paper Trail Media, az Organized Crime and Corruption Reporting Project (OCCRP), valamint a Cyprus Investigative Reporting Network – 2023 óta dolgozzák fel a kiszivárgott iratokat. Korábban a BBC és a TBIJ arról is beszámolt, hogy egy adózási konstrukció révén Abramovics több millió fontnyi adó megfizetését kerülhette el jachtjai üzemeltetési költségei után. A korábbi feltárás nyomán két volt cégvezető ellen vádat emeltek Cipruson. A tervek szerint a jövő hónapban állnak bíróság elé egy 25 millió eurós áfaügyben.
